\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{વિચિત્ર} (vicitra)}{વિચિત્ર (vicitra)}]{\gu{વિચિત્ર} (vicitra) — strange; odd}

\label{lesson:GU-C469-vicitra}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for boasting, then the Gujarati for to beguile.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{વિચિત્ર}}
\textbf{\gu{વિચિત્ર}} — \emph{vicitra} — \textquotedblleft{}strange; odd\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મારા} \gu{કાકાને} \gu{વિચિત્ર} \gu{ટેવ} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mārā kākāne vicitra ṭev che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle has an odd habit.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{વિચિત્ર}} (\emph{vicitra}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{vicitra}, \textquotedblleft{}variegated, many-coloured\textquotedblright{}, as Monier-Williams records it; Gujarati uses it for anything out of the ordinary.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vicitra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{vicitra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{mārā kākāne vicitra ṭev che.} — My uncle has an odd habit.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Gujarati for boasting, then the Gujarati for to beguile, then say \emph{vicitra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \gu{વિચિત્ર} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Strange; odd\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{તરંગી} (tarangī)}{તરંગી (tarangī)}]{\gu{તરંગી} (tarangī) — whimsical}

\label{lesson:GU-C469-tarangi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for to beguile, then the Gujarati for odd.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{તરંગી}}
\textbf{\gu{તરંગી}} — \emph{tarangī} — \textquotedblleft{}whimsical\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{તરંગી} \gu{મામા} \gu{રોજ} \gu{નવી} \gu{યોજના} \gu{બનાવે} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{tarangī māmā roj navī yojnā banāve che.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My whimsical uncle makes a new plan every day.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{તરંગી}} (\emph{tarangī}) is built on \emph{taraṅg}, \textquotedblleft{}a wave\textquotedblright{}, from Sanskrit \emph{taraṃga}, \textquotedblleft{}a wave, a billow\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), with \emph{-ī}: a mind that rises and falls like waves.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઝનૂન} (jhanūn)}{ઝનૂન (jhanūn)}]{\gu{ઝનૂન} (jhanūn) — obsession; frenzy}

\label{lesson:GU-C469-jhanun}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for odd, then the Gujarati for whimsical.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઝનૂન}}
\textbf{\gu{ઝનૂન}} — \emph{jhanūn} — \textquotedblleft{}obsession; frenzy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\gu{મીરાને} \gu{ક્રિકેટનું} \gu{ઝનૂન} \gu{છે}.
\end{quote}

\emph{Mīrāne krikeṭnũ jhanūn che.}

\textbf{\gu{ઝનૂન}} (\emph{jhanūn}) is usually traced to Arabic \emph{junūn}, \textquotedblleft{}madness\textquotedblright{}, through Persian.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\gu{ઉદ્યમ} (udyam)}{ઉદ્યમ (udyam)}]{\gu{ઉદ્યમ} (udyam) — industry; steady effort}

\label{lesson:GU-C469-udyam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Gujarati for obsession, then the Gujarati for sluggish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \gu{ઉદ્યમ}}
\textbf{\gu{ઉદ્યમ}} — \emph{udyam} — \textquotedblleft{}industry; steady effort\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{udyamthī garīb māṇas paṇ amīr bane che.}

A masculine noun.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\gu{ઉદ્યમ}} (\emph{udyam}) is a tatsama, Sanskrit \emph{udyama}, \textquotedblleft{}lifting up\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}undertaking, exertion\textquotedblright{}, as Monier-Williams records it.
\end{cousinweb}
